content:
A woman who lost her husband in the September 11 terrorist attacks read out her late husband's name at a memorial ceremony at the World Trade Center site, while publicly demanding that American leaders confront the role of the Saudi Arabian government and force them to "stop lying."

"How is it possible that after 25 years, there is still no accountability for the role Saudi Arabia played in your murder?" Terri Strada said on Friday after reading out the name of her late husband, Tom Strada. Her call for accountability drew loud cheers and applause from the otherwise solemn crowd.

"For 25 years, administration after administration, including some of the leaders standing before us today, have chosen to protect the Saudis rather than stand with the 9/11 families," she continued. She spoke from a nationally broadcast podium, with all four living former U.S. presidents in attendance listening, and Vice President JD Vance also present.

"Betrayal after betrayal. President Trump can still change this. Tell the Saudis to stop lying. Tell them that if they want to be friends with America, they can no longer keep denying all of this, denying all the pain and all the destruction we have endured," she said.

In another segment afterwards, another victim's family member, after reading out the name of her late aunt Lisa Marie Terry, similarly urged Trump to confront Saudi Arabia's role.

"For 25 years, the deep state has been covering up the truth of what really happened 25 years ago on that day. President Trump, you are our last hope. While the victims' families are still alive and can still see, declassify those unredacted files implicating Saudi Arabia," her remarks drew applause.

Strada is the national president of "9/11 Families United," a group that describes itself as a coalition of victims' families and survivors seeking answers to long-standing unresolved questions about the attacks, including Saudi Arabia's role.

Fifteen of the 19 men who hijacked the four airliners that day were Saudi nationals, although Saudi Arabia has consistently denied any responsibility or state involvement in the attacks.

The 9/11 Commission's final report, published in 2004, found that the commission "found no evidence that the Saudi government as an institution or senior Saudi officials individually funded" al-Qaeda, the terrorist group that directly orchestrated the attacks. However, the commission also described Saudi Arabia as "a problematic ally in the fight against Islamic extremism."
